claims.claim: The openai/math catalogue contains 722 manuscripts organized into 372 families.
The model was posed approximately 4,000 problems; each result used on average three hours of ChatGPT Pro thinking compute.
The integer multiplication manuscript claims a deterministic O(n(lg n)^(1-kappa)) algorithm with kappa = 2^-182 on a fixed multitape Turing machine.
Harvey and van der Hoeven proved O(n log n) integer multiplication on a multitape Turing machine (Annals of Mathematics 2021).
A proven Omega(n log n) lower bound exists only for on-line multitape Turing machine multiplication (Paterson-Fischer-Meyer 1974).
The Omega(n lg n) lower bound for constant-degree Boolean multiplication circuits is conditional on the network coding conjecture.
Harvey and van der Hoeven showed integer multiplication is at least as hard as bit-matrix transposition on Turing machines.
Storage modification (pointer) machines multiply n-bit integers in linear time (Schonhage 1980).
The Lean manifest formalization.yaml lists 162 source papers and 185 declarations, with scope 'Partial progress.' and review status unchecked.
Family 109 (integer multiplication below n log n) has no Lean documentation page and no formalization.yaml entry.
The '235 of 372 families with a Lean page and 162 fully formalized' figure is a third-party count that mixes families and papers.
Family 003's Lean formalization proves a zero-free half-plane Re(s) > 7/8 for zeta and Dirichlet L-functions; the 11/12 writeup was human edited.
Family 107 claims omega <= 9/4 over C, below the 2024 published record of about 2.371339.
AGMAI's guidelines asked that repositories not be controlled by any AI lab and that model name, prompts and summarized chain of thought be published.
AGMAI stated its involvement should not be interpreted as an endorsement of OpenAI's process.
An OpenAI spokesperson said almost every result came from a single prompt to a single agent and that OpenAI is not bound by the recommendations.
Thomas Bloom froze new proof claims on erdosproblems.com on 6 October 2026, citing a flood of AI-generated proof announcements.
Comparator checks statement match, permitted axioms and kernel acceptance, but trusts the challenge file's definitions.
Latent Space headlined '90 of the top 500 open math problems' without a visible source for the 90.
The earlier Navier-Stokes claim used roughly 10,000 concurrent agents for about 88 hours.
About 22% of the 722 manuscripts have a catalogued formalized main result (162 of 722).
assumptions: Each formalization.yaml source entry corresponds to one manuscript
